## Overview

`uniml` is arranged as a stack of small layers. The top-level
`run_workflow()` function wires them together, but each layer can also be
used directly. This vignette shows the atomic workflow with the package
example data.

The examples below are marked `eval = FALSE` where they train models or use
optional packages. They are intended as executable templates in an interactive
session with the suggested packages installed.

## Data and specification

The first step is to declare the binary outcome and the positive class.
Identifier and excluded columns are kept out of the modelling matrix.

```{r data-spec}
library(uniml)

data <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "uniml-example.csv", package = "uniml")
)
data$outcome <- factor(data$outcome, levels = c("no", "yes"))

spec <- uniml_spec(
  task_type = "binary",
  outcome = "outcome",
  positive = "yes",
  id = "id"
)

data <- as_uniml_data(data, spec)
names(data)
```

## Preprocessing

`fit_preprocessor()` learns imputation, scaling, and encoding parameters from
the training data. `apply_preprocessor()` applies those stored parameters to
new data without refitting.

```{r preprocessing}
spec <- set_preprocess(
  spec,
  impute = "median_mode",
  scale = "zscore",
  encode = "onehot"
)

preprocessor <- fit_preprocessor(data, spec = spec)
processed <- apply_preprocessor(preprocessor, data$data)

head(processed)
```

Use `scale = "minmax"` for range scaling, `encode = "onehot_drop"` to drop the
first dummy level, and `balance = "smote"` or `"rose"` when the training set
needs class balancing. Optional imputation methods include `"mice"`,
`"missForest"`, and `"missRanger"`.

## Feature selection

Multiple selection methods can be combined. The `k` argument controls
top-k methods such as random-forest importance and RFE. Collinearity pruning is
available through `cor_threshold` and `vif_threshold`.

```{r selection}
spec <- set_feature_selection(
  spec,
  methods = c("univariate", "lasso", "rf", "rfe"),
  combine = "intersect",
  k = 8,
  p_threshold = 0.2,
  cor_threshold = 0.9
)

selection <- select_features(processed, spec)
selection$selected_features
selection$details
```

Individual methods are also exported, for example `select_lasso()`,
`select_boruta()`, `select_rf_importance()`, `select_rfe()`,
`select_univariate()`, and `select_multivariate()`.

## Training and tuning

The same selection can be used to build an mlr3 task. Learner aliases are
resolved from the specification, then tuned and trained with the selected
features.

```{r training}
features <- intersect(selection$selected_features, names(processed))
task <- make_task(processed[, c(features, "outcome"), drop = FALSE], spec)

spec <- set_learners(spec, c("lr", "rf", "cart"), tune = TRUE)
learners <- resolve_learners(spec, task = task, n_train = task$nrow)

tuned <- tune_model(
  task,
  learners[["lr"]],
  resampling = mlr3::rsmp("cv", folds = 3),
  tuner = "random_search",
  terminator = mlr3tuning::trm("evals", n_evals = 5),
  seed = 123
)

model <- train_model(task, tuned$learner, params = tuned$best_params)
model
```

## Metrics and confidence intervals

Predictions can be evaluated with a fixed threshold or with the package
threshold helpers. Bootstrap confidence intervals resample paired
probabilities and labels.

```{r metrics}
prediction <- model$predict(task)
metrics <- calc_metrics(prediction, threshold = 0.5)
metrics

ci <- calc_ci(
  prediction$prob[, "yes"],
  prediction$truth,
  method = "bootstrap",
  R = 200,
  threshold = 0.5,
  positive = "yes",
  seed = 123
)
ci
```

The evaluation layer also includes calibration, DeLong and
Hosmer-Lemeshow tests, NRI/IDI, decision-curve analysis, and threshold
selection. See `set_evaluation()` and the corresponding help pages for
configuration details.

## Plots

The plotting functions accept a trained prediction, a collection of
predictions, or a `uniml_result`.

```{r plots}
plot_roc(prediction)
plot_calibration(prediction)
plot_confusion(prediction, threshold = 0.5)
plot_dca(dca(
  prediction$prob[, "yes"],
  prediction$truth,
  positive = "yes"
))
```

All performance plots share `theme_uniml()` and use the package palette
helpers. A model comparison figure can be produced after results are assembled
with `assemble_result()` or `run_workflow()`.
